summary: The app's own sketch solver now answers sketches and drags near a singular configuration, such as a point a little off where its circle touches its line, which it previously left to PlaneGCS or rejected. Rank there is too close to call at the solver's dependence distance. A row whose insertion into the rank factor, or whose witness fit, cannot be decided is now left out of the factor, which is unchanged by it, so later rows are decided as before; a smallest singular value estimate below 1e-7 also leaves rank unclear. A converged group with unclear rank is diagnosed uncertain: the dependencies found are labelled, but more may exist, so freedom is unknown. Such a group skips the move toward the solution nearest its start, and the app does not round its values to short decimals, which could close a near tangency exactly. The app solves it with freedom unknown, which the sketch panel already shows. Groups that did not converge are diagnosed as before, and a diagnosis that runs out of work is still unavailable. A drag can also end on a singular configuration, as one landing exactly on a tangency, where rank reads redundant though the sketch is not. A reached or projected drag whose end has more lasting relations dependent within ten times the dependence distance than its start had within it now walks back through its last eight accepted iterates and bisects toward the end with restored points, for the point closest to the targets that is no more singular than the start. That drag is reported limited, a new outcome between projected and stalled, unless the point is still within reach of the targets; work running out there restores the start and reports the group too large. On a 10 mm circle touching x = 10 the drag stops 1.4e-8 mm short of the tangency, 1.4e-7 mm on a 100 mm circle and 1.4e-6 mm on a 1000 mm one, and the sketch it leaves solves, drags and edits again. The app also no longer rounds a solved value by more than the solver's 1e-10 driver tolerance: far from the origin 8 ulps exceed it, and rounding could move a value further than the solver resolved. The native buffer protocol moves from 3 to 4 for the uncertain diagnosis and the limited drag outcome.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Sketches near a tangency, and drags that end on one, now solve with the app's own solver, with freedom unknown where rank is too close to call; drags onto an exact tangency stop a few nanometres to micrometres short of it. Values solved far from the origin keep digits the app used to round away when that rounding moved them by more than 1e-10 mm. The native solver's buffer format moves to protocol 4, which the app's bundled module and reader share.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage or journal schema change. The native solver buffer protocol moves from 3 to 4: diagnosis code 4 (uncertain, with labels and no freedom) and drag outcome code 3 (limited). Solved worker replies may now carry unknown freedom. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and result fields.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Rust tests drag a point onto a circle's tangency with x = r for radii 10, 100 and 1000 from lifts of 1e-3 and 1e-5 of the radius, twice: each drag is limited, accepted, blames nothing and stops within 2e-9 of the radius; the sketch it leaves solves in place, and moving the line to r - 1 solves at the expected point with freedom 0. A limited group beside a stalled one reports stalled. A two-link arm stretched past its reach and back over 47 frames, from the start and chained, has every frame converged, reached or projected, blaming nothing, with freedom 2 for every reached frame, and solves again where each frame left it. A distance repeated beside a near tangency is redundant whether it comes before or after the tangency, and a weakly held direction is uncertain rather than unavailable. A landing polish that runs out of work still leaves the landing as it was. Runtime tests run the same tangency lifecycle through the native-only app runtime for all three radii, keep native's own drag rejection where PlaneGCS does no better, solve an uncertain diagnosis with freedom unknown and without rounding, keep values far from the origin that rounding would move by more than 1e-10, and read limited outcomes and uncertain diagnoses with and without freedom. The protocol tests accept a solved reply with unknown freedom and refuse negative freedom. The workload benchmark test still compares every fixture between PlaneGCS and native only with the same four reviewed differences; native only now answers all 47 arm frames (3 were unavailable) and lands the tangency trajectory natively (it was diagnosed redundant); its 3 stalled tangency frames remain, for the next release.
